rationale: The run produced output/table1_1948_2010.json (in the codebase output/ dir) with four of Table 1's five columns, computed on the reconstructed 1948-2010 series via the footnote-11 HP(1e5)/regression decomposition described in plan steps 3 and 5. Job-finding contributions reproduce the paper closely: col1 1948-2010 0.7632 vs 0.77 (0.9%), col2 1967-2010 0.8067 vs 0.83 (2.8%), col3 1976-2010 0.8382 vs 0.85 (1.4%), col4 1987-2010 0.8584 vs 0.90 (4.6%) — all within 5%. The employment-exit contributions drift outward for the smaller values: 0.2453 vs 0.24 (2.2%, match), 0.1984 vs 0.17 (16.7%, partial band), 0.1658 vs 0.15 (10.5%, partial band), and 0.1437 vs 0.10 (43.7%, beyond 30%). The fifth column, men 25-54 1976-2010 (paper 0.69/0.32), was never produced: no demographic/prime-age series exists anywhere in output/ or the codebase (grep for '25-54'/'prime' found nothing), and plan steps 3 and 5 explicitly scoped the run to 'the columns computable from whole-population aggregate data,' excluding the microdata-based prime-age sample. The specific check that col5 finding (0.69) exceed twice col5 exit (0.32) therefore cannot be evaluated. fix_severity.json notes one major fix (a --splice_tail extension to reach the 2010 endpoint), which underlies the full-sample series used here. With half the finding cells matching, exit cells spread across the partial and no-match bands, and one full column absent, the overall verdict is partial.
